items.title: R1 Durable Safe Core
items.description: Deliver a restart-safe local orchestrator with versioned authority, independent evidence, normalized agents, leases, and bounded persistent loops.
acceptance_criteria: Existing 0.1.x SQLite state upgrades without losing accepted state or audit history.
A forced restart resumes authorized work without duplicating an external mutation.
Every accepted criterion resolves to immutable independently verified evidence.
review_notes: Human authority must approve any migration that can alter or discard accepted mission state.

items.title: Versioned domain model and compatibility migration
items.description: Separate durable Control Plane identities and lifecycle state while preserving the current SQLite authority and deferring multi-tenancy until the single-node coding loop is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Work item, run, stage, assignment, worker session, attempt, lease, worktree, and artifact have separate immutable identities.
A migration upgrades the current SQLite database without losing approvals, attempts, events, or artifacts.
Every lifecycle transition is checked by an explicit state machine.
The work-item payload is no longer the sole storage location for authoritative domain state.
review_notes: A human database owner reviews the compatibility and rollback evidence before release.

items.title: Transactional event outbox and tamper-evident audit chain
items.description: Persist state transitions and outbound events atomically, then chain audit records so modification is detectable.
acceptance_criteria: A state transition and its corresponding outbox event commit in one transaction under fault injection.
Repeated event delivery cannot create a duplicate external action.
Changing or deleting an audit record is detected by integrity verification.
Every event carries correlation identities for mission, task, run, stage, attempt, and worker session.

items.title: Content-addressed artifact and criterion-evidence ledger
items.description: Separate working, candidate, accepted, evidence, released, and quarantined artifacts and bind acceptance criteria to immutable evidence manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Every artifact records a SHA-256 digest, producer, verifier, inputs, and toolchain.
Every acceptance criterion links to concrete test results, diffs, or review evidence.
An LLM summary without primary evidence cannot close a criterion.
Accepted evidence is immutable and fails verification after modification.

items.title: Deterministic policy plane, autonomy modes, and emergency stop
items.description: Evaluate capabilities, risk tiers, autonomy levels, approvals, budgets, and tripwires outside model reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: The same normalized request and policy version produce the same allow, deny, or require-approval decision.
Emergency stop prevents new dispatches and cancels active mutable worker sessions.
An approval is bound to the exact task, stage, worker, runtime, worktree, permissions, and definition digest.
Hermes cannot bypass Control Plane policy through its own tool, skill, session, or subagent.
review_notes: Only an authorized human may approve high-risk actions, lift emergency stop, or accept a policy exception.

items.title: Normalized adapter contract, qualification, and agent lifecycle
items.description: Bring every provider behind one lifecycle-capable adapter contract and qualify declared capabilities with evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Codex, Claude, Gemini, Antigravity, Ollama, and deterministic adapters pass the same contract test suite for supported operations.
Health distinguishes availability, reliability, quality, safety, performance, cost, freshness, and drift.
A failed worker is drained or quarantined, a compatible qualified replacement is selected, and a complete handoff record is preserved for the recovery controller.

items.title: Durable workflow execution, checkpoints, and resume
items.description: Execute versioned workflow stages through committed checkpoints and restart-safe state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Every stage persists pending, running, waiting_approval, succeeded, or failed state.
After restart, a workflow resumes from its last committed checkpoint.
Retry does not duplicate a provider call, worktree, or GitHub operation.
The workflow version is pinned for every run.
review_notes: A human approver remains a first-class durable workflow signal and cannot be simulated by an agent.

items.title: Dependency scheduler, TTL/fenced leases, and conflict domains
items.description: Schedule ready tasks from the dependency graph while preventing stale workers and conflicting mutations.
acceptance_criteria: Only leaf tasks with completed dependencies become runnable; epics and stories are never dispatched as coding tasks.
A claim creates a durable assignment, TTL lease, and fencing token.
A stale worker cannot write an artifact or commit after losing its lease.
Independent conflict domains run concurrently while overlapping file or module mutations serialize or escalate.

items.title: Persistent Loop Engineering and no-progress control
items.description: Persist a bounded implementation, validation, critic, and repair loop whose authoritative state survives transcript loss and process restart.
acceptance_criteria: Every iteration persists objective, plan, diff, validator results, critic result, and budget usage.
Iteration, time, token, cost, and tool-failure limits stop or pause the loop deterministically.
The same failure twice consecutively triggers replan or policy-selected worker replacement.
The loop terminates only through accepted evidence, explicit failure, or human escalation.
review_notes: Budget or iteration limit increases require the configured human approval at the applicable risk tier.

items.title: Worker Runtime abstraction
items.description: Introduce a lifecycle-aware worker runtime boundary; Hermes is not represented as an ordinary CLIProvider.
acceptance_criteria: The interface supports start, resume, heartbeat, cancel, collect_events, and finalize.
Direct CLI and Hermes ACP runtimes pass one shared contract test suite.
A runtime returns structured events, tool calls, artifacts, and terminal status.
Fallback is forbidden after the first mutable action.
Hermes one-shot mode is qualification-only or read-only because it bypasses interactive approvals; mutable sessions use the ACP permission bridge.
review_notes: The Control Plane remains authoritative for policy, approvals, leases, evidence, and terminal acceptance.

items.title: Hermes adapter and session lifecycle
items.description: Bind Hermes ACP sessions to durable Control Plane identities, Control-Plane-owned worktrees, scoped context, tools, and cancellation authority.
acceptance_criteria: A Hermes session is bound to task, run, stage, attempt, agent role, and worktree identities.
The Control Plane starts Hermes as an ACP stdio child process, collects protocol events, resumes by stable session identity, and cancels the complete process tree.
The approved worktree is passed as the ACP working directory; Hermes does not create a second unmanaged worktree.
Hermes receives only a scoped context package and allowlisted tools.
Control Plane restart preserves Hermes session identity.
Executable discovery, version constraints, hermes-acp --check, and workspace access are explicit health and qualification evidence; absence or incompatibility fails closed.

items.title: Per-stage live execution approvals
items.description: Make live workflow stages wait durably for an exact approval and continue automatically after the approved logical attempt.
acceptance_criteria: A live stage enters waiting_approval without failing the workflow.
An approved gate is delivered only to its exact stage execution and consumed by one logical attempt.
A rejected or expired gate cannot start Hermes or another worker runtime.
A completed stage advances automatically to the next dependency-ready stage.
review_notes: Hermes cannot synthesize, widen, or consume a human approval outside its exact scope.

items.title: Execution Context Package MVP
items.description: Create an immutable, bounded dispatch package before the full role-aware context broker.
acceptance_criteria: Every dispatch receives an immutable context digest.
The package contains task, acceptance criteria, dependencies, base SHA, policies, relevant requirements, and previous decisions.
Included, excluded, and superseded sources are explicit.
Token and size limits use deterministic compaction.

items.title: Minimal execution telemetry and enforced budgets
items.description: Correlate the single-node execution loop and enforce token, cost, stage, retry, and tool budgets before OpenTelemetry export.
acceptance_criteria: One correlation root connects task, workflow, Hermes session, worker process, worktree, validators, and approvals.
Duration, retries, tokens, estimated cost, tool calls, and terminal reason are retained.
Maximum tokens, cost, and stage budgets actually block or pause execution.
The dashboard shows active sessions, queue, leases, worktrees, failures, and budget state.

items.title: Local recovery and orphan reconciliation
items.description: Recover single-node coding-loop authority and reconcile orphaned runtime sessions, processes, leases, and worktrees.
acceptance_criteria: Restart restores stage, lease, Hermes session reference, context digest, worktree, and pending approval.
Orphaned provider processes, Hermes sessions, and worktrees are detected separately.
A stale worker cannot commit after a newer fencing token is issued.
Process termination at each local mutation boundary creates no duplicate commit or external operation.
Restore verifies artifact digests and audit continuity.
review_notes: Destructive reconciliation remains a human-authorized Control Plane action.

items.title: R2 Mission Factory
items.description: Analyze a free-form mission, compose a justified workforce, approve a versioned Factory Blueprint, and bootstrap resumable execution.
acceptance_criteria: A natural-language mission reaches a deterministic readiness verdict with unresolved questions and authority sources recorded.
The composed workforce and Blueprint expose rejected alternatives, qualifications, risks, and verification strategy.
Human Blueprint approval bootstraps the mission idempotently without project-specific core logic.
review_notes: A human mission owner approves the Blueprint and all subsequent authority-changing amendments.

items.title: Mission intake, source authority, clarifications, and readiness verdict
items.description: Normalize mission intent, distinguish authoritative from advisory inputs, detect gaps, and issue a readiness state.
acceptance_criteria: Intake emits one allowed readiness verdict with a machine-readable rationale and blocking gaps.
Every source is classified by authority, version, provenance, and conflict status.
Ambiguous, infeasible, or high-risk missions produce clarification or review requests and cannot silently proceed.
review_notes: Only the human mission owner may resolve intent ambiguity or accept a materially reduced scope.

items.title: Provider-neutral Role Definitions and compatibility contracts
items.description: Represent responsibilities, inputs, outputs, tools, independence, limits, and qualifications as versioned role contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Role definitions validate typed inputs, outputs, tools, permissions, limits, evidence contracts, and incompatible duties.
Role versions remain provider-neutral and can be resolved independently from agent definitions.
Workflows reference role requirements rather than concrete agent IDs.
Compatibility tests reject one agent serving mutually exclusive implementer and final-review duties in the same decision.

items.title: Evaluation-aware Agent Router, independent reviewer rotation, and qualification history
items.description: Rank eligible agents by proven capability, risk, quality, latency, cost, diversity, current health, and independent-review history while recording rationale.
acceptance_criteria: Each routing decision records eligible and excluded candidates, capability, qualification, model independence, cost, latency, load, rationale, and selected fallback chain.
An agent with expired or failed qualification cannot receive a task requiring that qualification.
Existing model-aware reviewer rotation remains preserved and deterministic.
Pinned, best-qualified, cost-aware, latency-aware, diversity, canary, tournament, and fallback strategies have deterministic tests.

items.title: Role pools, arbitration strategies, and Workforce Composer
items.description: Build role pools and generate a justified workforce from mission needs, policy, budget, independence, and provider diversity.
acceptance_criteria: The composer emits required roles, pool strategy, minimum and maximum replicas, qualifications, and fallback assignments.
A strengthened role can use at least two heterogeneous qualified agents with an explicit arbitration rule.
Missing capability, independence, capacity, or budget produces a visible gap instead of an invalid workforce.
review_notes: A human reviews workforce exceptions that weaken required independence or provider diversity.

items.title: Factory Blueprint generation, alternatives, approval, and amendments
items.description: Generate the mandatory versioned operating design for modules, workforce, tools, context, verification, budgets, policies, and recovery.
acceptance_criteria: A Blueprint validates every required section and traces decisions to mission sources, risks, assumptions, and rejected alternatives.
Execution remains blocked until the configured human signs the exact Blueprint version and digest.
An amendment creates a new immutable version with impact analysis and preserves prior approvals and execution history.
review_notes: Blueprint approval and authority-changing amendments are reserved for the human mission owner.

items.title: Idempotent mission bootstrap, manifests, and rollback point
items.description: Instantiate an approved Blueprint into mission state, queues, manifests, policies, budgets, and a recoverable initial checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated bootstrap with the same Blueprint digest creates one mission and one initial workflow graph.
Bootstrap persists exact agent, role, tool, policy, context, budget, and environment manifests.
A failed bootstrap compensates partial resources and restores the recorded pre-bootstrap rollback point.

items.title: Immutable Context Packages, provenance, broker, and compaction
items.description: Build minimal task-specific context packages with authority, provenance, freshness, token budgets, and deterministic compaction.
acceptance_criteria: Every dispatched task references an immutable context package digest and records included, excluded, and superseded sources.
The broker enforces configured token and freshness limits while preserving authoritative requirements and safety constraints.
Compaction tests retain decisions, unresolved risks, evidence references, and next-step state after raw transcript removal.

items.title: Typed memory, bounded retrieval, invalidation, and governed skills
items.description: Store durable facts, decisions, procedures, outcomes, and skills in typed memory managed by explicit curation policy.
acceptance_criteria: Memory writes declare type, scope, source, confidence, validity interval, and invalidation conditions.
Working, semantic, episodic, procedural, entity, contextual, preference, and raw-history stores remain separately queryable and enforce their own write policies.
Retrieval is bounded by tenant, mission, task purpose, authority, freshness, and maximum result count.
A stale or contradicted memory entry is invalidated without deleting its provenance or historical consumers.
A generated skill cannot advance from draft to approved until versioned tests, security review, and representative evaluation thresholds pass; it can later be deprecated or revoked.
review_notes: Promoting agent output into an authoritative reusable skill requires the configured curator or human approval.

items.title: Software engineering role pack
items.description: Define provider-neutral typed contracts for the initial software delivery roles after validator and routing foundations exist.
acceptance_criteria: The pack defines Requirements and Backlog Steward, Solution Architect, Implementation Worker, Deterministic Test Runner, Independent Code Reviewer, Security Reviewer, Release and Integration Agent, and Policy Guardian roles.
Every role has a typed input and output contract.
Validator and reviewer remain separate roles.
An implementer cannot accept its own result.
The Release Agent can operate only on approved candidate artifacts.

items.title: R3 Safe Extensibility
items.description: Execute untrusted work inside narrow environments, broker tools and credentials, verify independently, govern change, and install capabilities without editing core.
acceptance_criteria: An allowlisted MCP tool executes through policy, sandbox, credential, audit, and artifact boundaries.
Adversarial instructions cannot widen authority and produce a recorded tripwire or quarantine event.
A signed pack installs and rolls back without core edits, and its work is independently verified.
review_notes: Humans retain approval authority for protected connectors, architecture decisions, credential scope, and release acceptance.

items.title: Local sandbox subset for writable workers
items.description: Restrict a writable worker to its task worktree and declared temporary paths with process, time, output, and network controls enforced outside prompts.
acceptance_criteria: A writable worker can access only its task worktree and declared temporary paths.
A write outside the worktree is blocked and audited.
Process, time, output, and network limits are enforced outside prompt-level instructions.
Sandbox teardown preserves evidence and the candidate diff.

items.title: Tool Registry, Tool Gateway, MCP manager, and connector lifecycle
items.description: Normalize tools and MCP servers behind policy-enforced discovery, validation, invocation, health, and revocation.
acceptance_criteria: Every tool descriptor declares schemas, side effects, risk tier, required capabilities, timeouts, and evidence outputs.
Dynamic discovery never grants invocation authority beyond the mission, role, and policy allowlists.
Connector install, health failure, disable, upgrade, and removal are auditable and covered by lifecycle tests.
review_notes: A human approves registration or scope expansion for mutation-capable production connectors.

items.title: Short-lived scoped credential broker with zero prompt/log exposure
items.description: Issue narrowly scoped ephemeral credentials directly to approved tools without exposing secret material to agents, prompts, artifacts, or logs.
acceptance_criteria: Issued credentials are bound to one tenant, mission, tool, operation set, and expiration time.
Automated scans find no credential values in prompts, model output, audit records, traces, exceptions, or artifacts.
Revocation prevents subsequent use and produces an auditable lifecycle event without revealing the secret.
review_notes: A human system owner approves scopes above the mission's pre-approved credential policy.

items.title: Independent evaluation service and criterion verdicts
items.description: Run deterministic checks before model-assisted review and produce independent criterion-level verdicts over primary evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic checks execute before any LLM review.
A reviewer cannot use the model that produced the candidate change.
A verdict records rubric version, criterion evidence, confidence, concerns, and dissent.
Acceptance fails when any required criterion lacks primary evidence.
review_notes: Human authority remains the final verification layer for configured high-impact outcomes.

items.title: Prompt-injection red team, tripwires, quarantine, and incidents
items.description: Continuously test hostile inputs and activate deterministic containment when instructions attempt to bypass authority or exfiltrate data.
acceptance_criteria: A maintained corpus covers indirect injection, authority escalation, secret extraction, tool abuse, artifact poisoning, and cross-tenant access.
Every seeded attack is denied or contained and produces a linked tripwire, quarantine, or incident record.
A seeded evidence-tampering attempt is blocked, preserves the original evidence, and opens a security incident linked to the actor, attempt, and affected criterion.
A quarantined output cannot enter accepted context, memory, artifacts, or downstream execution until explicitly released.
review_notes: Only an authorized human security reviewer may release quarantined high-risk content or close a material incident.

items.title: ADR governance and transactional Blueprint impact propagation
items.description: Record architecture changes as decisions, calculate their impact, and update affected Blueprint and workflow contracts transactionally.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR records context, alternatives, decision, consequences, affected contracts, evidence, and approval status.
Impact analysis identifies affected tasks, context packages, policies, evaluations, artifacts, and deployment assumptions before activation.
Applying an approved ADR creates a new Blueprint version atomically or leaves the prior version fully active.
review_notes: An authorized human architecture owner approves ADRs that change mission authority, safety, data, or external contracts.

items.title: Audited parallel, generator-critic, quorum, debate, and red/blue patterns
items.description: Provide bounded parallel, generator-critic, quorum, debate, tournament, and red-blue coordination as explicit workflow patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Each pattern declares participants, model-aware reviewer rotation, independence constraints, turn and budget limits, arbitration, termination, and required evidence.
All inter-agent contributions flow through typed stored artifacts or events rather than unlogged free-form conversation.
Tests demonstrate deterministic termination and dissent preservation for every supported arbitration strategy.

items.title: Signed pack SDK and install/upgrade/disable/rollback manager
items.description: Define versioned extension contracts for domain, capability, connector, policy, evaluation, and UI packs with supply-chain controls.
acceptance_criteria: Pack manifests declare identity, version, compatibility, permissions, dependencies, migrations, evaluations, and signature metadata.
Install and upgrade reject invalid signatures, incompatible core versions, undeclared permissions, and failed qualification tests.
Disable and rollback restore the previous working version without editing factory core or losing mission history.
review_notes: A human administrator approves trust roots and any pack requesting mutation-capable or privileged connectors.

items.title: Software Engineering reference pack and release evidence
items.description: Package the proven worktree, worker, validator, review, and release contracts as a product-neutral installable capability after the single-node coding loop works.
acceptance_criteria: The pack consumes the core worktree and candidate-artifact contracts without reimplementing them.
Every change traces to a requirement, task, Blueprint decision or ADR, test evidence, and independent review verdict.
The pack produces a reproducible release manifest, dependency and security evidence, and a tested rollback procedure.
review_notes: Only the configured human release authority may approve publication or merge to a protected branch.

items.title: Hermes qualification and controlled fallback
items.description: Qualify Hermes lifecycle and restrictions while retaining bounded direct CLI fallback for compatible read-only work.
acceptance_criteria: Qualification verifies executable resolution, version constraints, hermes-acp --check, session lifecycle, cancellation, workspace confinement, tool restrictions, permission bridging, usage reporting, and the artifact contract.
A failed Hermes runtime can be quarantined.
Direct Codex or Claude remains a controlled fallback only for compatible read-only tasks before any mutable action.
A mutable session cannot move between runtimes without an explicit checkpoint and new lease.

items.title: Worktree manager
items.description: Move core worktree isolation from AF-025 into the P0 Control Plane coding path.
acceptance_criteria: Each task attempt receives a deterministic branch and isolated worktree from an approved base SHA.
Concurrent tasks cannot mutate the same worktree.
Metadata records repository, base SHA, branch, task, lease, and owner.
The Control Plane is the sole worktree authority; managed Hermes sessions receive the existing worktree and never invoke Hermes worktree creation.
Startup reconciliation finds orphaned, dirty, and missing worktrees.
Cleanup occurs only after terminal state and the configured retention period.

items.title: Codex CLI implementation worker
items.description: Run a qualified writable Codex worker only inside its leased task worktree.
acceptance_criteria: Codex can modify only the task worktree.
Invocation uses fixed arguments and a reviewed permission profile.
The result records changed files, diff digest, commands, exit state, and handoff.
The worker cannot merge, push, close an issue, or grant final approval.
Timeout or cancellation terminates the complete process tree.

items.title: Claude Code implementation worker
items.description: Provide a separately qualified writable Claude Code profile compatible with the implementation-worker contract.
acceptance_criteria: Claude Code can modify only the task worktree and passes its own qualification matrix.
Plan-only Claude roles remain separate from the writable implementation profile.
Provider replacement does not change the task or workflow contract.
Codex and Claude replace one another only when role qualification is compatible.
Timeout or cancellation terminates the complete process tree.

items.title: Candidate change artifact and approval-gated PR plan
items.description: Represent a worker result as immutable candidate-change evidence before any push or pull-request mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate artifact records base and head SHA, diff digest, changed files, and worktree identity.
The commit message includes the stable task ID.
Push and pull-request creation remain dry-run or separately approval-gated.
The base branch is never changed directly.
Failed validation cannot enter PR-ready state.
review_notes: AF-050 may satisfy the implementation-worker dependency after compatible qualification.

items.title: Deterministic validator runner
items.description: Run project-pack tests, lint, type checks, builds, and security scans in the candidate worktree through fixed command vectors.
acceptance_criteria: Only allowlisted command vectors execute and no shell is used.
A project pack declares test, lint, type-check, build, and security-scan commands.
Each result records command digest, exit code, bounded output, and environment metadata.
Validation runs in the candidate worktree rather than the main checkout.
Test evidence maps to acceptance criteria.

items.title: End-to-end coding delivery loop
items.description: Connect claim, worktree, implementation, validation, independent review, repair, founder decision, and PR planning as one idempotent vertical slice; AF-057 supplies crash-boundary recovery qualification.
acceptance_criteria: A ready task proceeds through claim, worktree, implement, validate, review, and founder decision.
Test failure returns to the same worker or a policy-selected compatible replacement.
The maximum repair iteration count is deterministic.
Success produces a PR-ready plan but never auto-merges.
Replaying the same logical attempt at supported checkpoints creates no duplicate worktree, commit, or provider mutation.
review_notes: Founder acceptance remains separate from worker and reviewer terminal status.

items.title: R4 Operable Platform
items.description: Expose one governed service boundary, make missions observable and recoverable, isolate tenants, and provide a usable human control plane.
acceptance_criteria: CLI, SDK, web UI, and webhooks use one versioned API and policy boundary.
A root trace links mission intake through cost, decisions, execution, evidence, and final authority.
Restart and adversarial isolation tests show no duplicate mutation, accepted-state loss, or cross-tenant observation.
review_notes: Human operators retain explicit approval, pause, resume, stop, incident, and exception controls.

items.title: REST operations API, idempotency/ETags, webhooks, and SDK contracts
items.description: Expose all supported orchestration and control operations through one authenticated, versioned, concurrency-safe service boundary.
acceptance_criteria: An OpenAPI contract covers registry, missions, workflows, approvals, evidence, events, incidents, budgets, and operations.
Mutation endpoints enforce idempotency keys and conditional updates reject stale ETags with a conflict response.
Signed webhooks retry idempotently and the generated SDK passes contract tests against the service.

items.title: OpenTelemetry and cost ledger
items.description: Export the minimal execution telemetry through OpenTelemetry and extend it with provider-reported and estimated cost accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Traces export through OpenTelemetry without changing correlation identities.
Metrics include queue depth, wait time, run duration, failure rate, iteration count, and orphaned resources.
The ledger supports provider-reported and estimated usage.
Budget thresholds can notify, reroute, pause, or require approval.
review_notes: Only the configured human budget authority may increase a hard mission budget after execution begins.

items.title: Full chaos recovery and verified restore
items.description: Extend the local AF-057 recovery subset across host, network, queue, clustered deployment, and storage faults.
acceptance_criteria: Clustered recovery preserves stage, lease, runtime session, context, worktree, budget, approval, and external-operation identities.
Chaos tests terminate hosts and services at every mutation boundary without duplicate commits or external operations.
A documented restore exercise meets the configured recovery targets and verifies accepted artifact and audit-chain integrity.
review_notes: A human operator approves destructive reconciliation or rollback that could supersede accepted external state.

items.title: PostgreSQL/object storage migration and end-to-end tenant isolation
items.description: Move transactional authority and binary artifacts to production stores while enforcing tenant isolation through every access path.
acceptance_criteria: The migration preserves record counts, versions, digests, relationships, and audit-chain verification from SQLite and local artifacts.
Database, object, cache, queue, search, telemetry, and connector access all require an explicit tenant scope.
Adversarial isolation tests cannot read, infer, mutate, enumerate, or trigger side effects for a different tenant.
Data classification, handling, residency, retention, and legal-hold rules are enforced consistently across authoritative state, artifacts, memory, search, backups, logs, and exports.
Per-tenant quotas plus verified export and deletion workflows produce criterion-level completion evidence without bypassing retention or legal hold.
review_notes: A human data owner approves cutover after backup and restore evidence has passed.

items.title: Human Control Plane for evidence, approvals, incidents, cost, and intervention
items.description: Provide an accessible web control plane for mission oversight, evidence inspection, approvals, interventions, incidents, and spend.
acceptance_criteria: Users can inspect mission status, provenance, evidence, dissent, cost, policy decisions, leases, and incidents without database access.
Approve, reject, pause, resume, cancel, recompose, release, and emergency-stop actions require authenticated role authority and are audited.
The API and UI can enable, pause, drain, quarantine, replace, and irreversibly retire an Agent Definition version with policy checks and lifecycle evidence.
Keyboard-only and screen-reader checks pass the declared accessibility baseline for all approval and emergency paths.
review_notes: The interface must never offer an agent the ability to impersonate or synthesize a human approval.

items.title: Single-node, clustered, hybrid, and air-gapped deployment definitions
items.description: Publish reproducible deployment profiles with health, scaling, upgrade, backup, and security defaults for supported topologies.
acceptance_criteria: Automated smoke tests deploy and verify single-node and clustered profiles from versioned manifests.
Hybrid and air-gapped profiles document and enforce allowed egress, model, connector, update, and artifact-transfer paths.
A rolling upgrade and rollback preserve active mission authority, pending approvals, accepted artifacts, and audit continuity.
review_notes: A human operator approves production deployment, upgrade, rollback, and any air-gap transfer.

items.title: R0.2 Local Control Center MVP
items.description: Expose the current Agent Factory state and guarded operator actions through a lightweight local web interface without duplicating orchestration logic or waiting for the production control plane.
acceptance_criteria: A Windows operator starts the control center with one documented command and sees current projects, work items, runs, agents, providers, approvals, and recent events.
Every mutation available in the MVP calls the same application services and policy checks as the CLI and creates an audit event.
The UI never auto-approves final acceptance, auto-merges, auto-closes, or silently changes GitHub state.
review_notes: The founder remains the final authority; independent reviewer recommendations are displayed but cannot synthesize founder approval.

items.title: Shared application-service boundary for CLI and web
items.description: Extract operator queries and guarded commands behind reusable Python services so the CLI and web interface cannot diverge in behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Projects, work items, runs, agents, providers, reviews, approvals, events, and settings have typed query results independent of terminal formatting.
Every supported mutation passes through the existing policy, approval, storage, and audit path rather than invoking a shell command from the web server.
Contract tests execute equivalent CLI and service operations and observe the same state transitions and audit events.

items.title: Local FastAPI host and read-only operations API
items.description: Provide a loopback-only web process with typed read endpoints, health reporting, bounded pagination, and safe startup defaults.
acceptance_criteria: The documented command starts on 127.0.0.1 by default and serves health plus typed read endpoints for every MVP dashboard resource.
List endpoints use bounded pagination and return explicit unavailable or stale states instead of hiding provider and GitHub failures.
API tests cover valid, empty, malformed, missing, and concurrent-read cases against a temporary SQLite database.

items.title: Live development dashboard and navigation shell
items.description: Build the local dashboard that summarizes delivery progress, active work, blocked work, provider health, pending decisions, and recent failures.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard shows counts and direct links for ready, active, blocked, failed, awaiting-review, and awaiting-approval work.
Agent and provider status, current workflow stages, pending approvals, and recent failures refresh without a full page reload.
Empty, loading, stale, disconnected, and error states remain readable and never appear as successful execution.

items.title: Backlog, work-item, and workflow run controls
items.description: Expose backlog inspection and the currently supported guarded workflow commands with dependency, stage, evidence, and blocker visibility.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can filter work items by project, type, status, priority, dependency, and assignee and inspect acceptance criteria and linked artifacts.
Supported claim, simulation-run, review, and workflow-run actions show a confirmation summary and preserve all existing execution gates.
A run detail view displays ordered stages, selected agents and models, verdicts, evidence, errors, and the exact reason progression stopped.
review_notes: The MVP exposes only commands already supported safely by the application service; unsupported cancel or resume operations are shown as unavailable rather than simulated.

items.title: Agent, provider, and reviewer routing controls
items.description: Let the operator inspect provider health and safely enable, disable, replace, and configure agent assignments and reviewer rotation.
acceptance_criteria: The UI displays each agent role, provider, model, enabled state, recent assignment, reviewer usage, and provider health without exposing credentials.
Enable, disable, and replace actions validate role compatibility, show their impact, require confirmation, and write an audit event.
Reviewer views prove the selected reviewer differs from every reviewed producer model and explain exclusions and rotation history.

items.title: Review inbox and founder approval workspace
items.description: Present implementation artifacts, tests, criterion evidence, independent reviewer verdicts, dissent, and final founder decisions in one workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Each pending decision shows the work-item acceptance criteria, implementation artifacts, validation results, independent reviewer identity, verdict, and unresolved findings.
Approve and reject actions require an explicit confirmation and optional note, are idempotent, and record actor, timestamp, target, previous state, and resulting state.
No reviewer verdict can activate the founder approval endpoint or cause merge, close, release, or GitHub mutation without a separate authorized founder action.
review_notes: Founder approval remains a separate human action even when every automated reviewer passes.

items.title: Audit explorer, runtime settings, and GitHub sync preview
items.description: Expose searchable event history, bounded operator settings, environment status, and the existing GitHub dry-run review and approval flow.
acceptance_criteria: The audit explorer filters by time, project, work item, run, agent, provider, action, and outcome and links records to related artifacts.
Editable settings are allowlisted, validated, versioned, and audited; secret values and unrestricted command arguments are never displayed or accepted.
GitHub sync defaults to dry-run, presents create and update operations plus the immutable plan digest, and requires the existing separate approval before apply.

items.title: Windows launch experience, accessibility, and end-to-end qualification
items.description: Make the MVP easy to start on the existing Windows workstation and prove the complete local operator path with automated and manual evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A documented PowerShell command installs optional web dependencies, starts the service, opens the local URL, and stops cleanly without requiring script-policy changes.

An end-to-end test imports a sample backlog, runs a deterministic workflow, routes an independent review, reaches founder approval, records the decision, and verifies the audit trail through the UI-facing API.
Keyboard navigation, focus visibility, labels, contrast, responsive layout, and critical screen-reader paths pass the documented MVP accessibility checklist.
review_notes: Completion requires founder confirmation that the dashboard exposes enough evidence to make a real acceptance decision.

items.title: R5 Production Qualification
items.description: Prove the platform against measurable service objectives and the reusable reference mission, then hand it over with recovery evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The qualification suite maps every final acceptance criterion to immutable stored evidence.
A 72-hour fault-injection soak loses no accepted state and keeps resource growth within defined bounds.
A heterogeneous reference mission and a second unrelated mission complete without core workflow changes.
review_notes: Only the designated human acceptance authority may sign the GA evidence bundle and final handover.

items.title: NFR, performance, accessibility, isolation, and recovery qualification suite
items.description: Automate evidence for availability, capacity, latency, durability, security, accessibility, isolation, and recovery objectives.
acceptance_criteria: The suite measures every declared NFR and SLO with thresholds, environment metadata, repeatable load profiles, and retained raw evidence.
Capacity tests sustain at least 10 active runs, 25 runnable tasks, and 100 registered agents without violating declared latency targets.
Accessibility, tenant-isolation, backup, and restore checks fail the qualification gate when any required result is absent or below threshold.
review_notes: A human product and operations owner approves any documented SLO exception before release.

items.title: 72-hour fault-injection soak with bounded resource growth
items.description: Run sustained mixed missions while injecting provider, worker, process, network, queue, storage, and host faults.
acceptance_criteria: The soak runs continuously for at least 72 hours with a versioned workload and fault schedule.
No accepted state, evidence, audit continuity, or authorized external-operation identity is lost or duplicated.
Memory, storage, queue depth, orphaned leases, and temporary environments stay within documented steady-state bounds.

items.title: Full heterogeneous-agent reference acceptance mission
items.description: Execute the specification reference mission through intake, Blueprint, heterogeneous workforce, guarded mutation, verification, recovery, and human acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: At least three heterogeneous qualified agent providers participate through replaceable role assignments and recorded routing rationale.
The mission demonstrates independent verification, one worker replacement, one recovery event, one approval gate, and a reproducible release artifact.
All 45 final acceptance criteria resolve to signed evidence or an explicitly human-accepted exception with rationale.
review_notes: The designated Mission Owner or acceptance authority performs the final mission verdict; no agent may self-accept the result.

items.title: Runbooks, clean install, restore exercise, GA evidence, and handover
items.description: Complete operational documentation, prove clean deployment and disaster recovery, assemble the evidence index, and transfer ownership.
acceptance_criteria: A new operator completes clean install, provider registration, mission start, emergency stop, backup, restore, and upgrade using only versioned runbooks.
The GA evidence index links every requirement, risk, acceptance criterion, test, artifact, decision, exception, and recovery exercise.
A second unrelated mission starts from a new Blueprint without changing factory core workflow code.
review_notes: The human release authority signs the GA evidence bundle and accepts operational handover.
